title: Build your first report
subtitle: A useful result. Clear boundaries. Evidence you can inspect.
courseLabel: Harness in practice · Tutorial 2 of 6 · Plan → Build

sections.title: Build a report you can explain
sections.intro: Turn six synthetic activity entries into a formatted report, while keeping the input and checks protected.
sections.html:
Open the formatted report. It accounts for 6 entries and 270 minutes. Orion has 180 minutes and Lumen has 90.

This lesson practices the current Harness 1.7.0 workflow with fixed local command participants. The worker supplies known reference code; the protocol reviewer does not judge its quality. The protected tests check the actual program. No model or provider is called.

For real implementation, your assistant needs participants suited to the task and the execution authority you choose. Start with the offline practice to understand the decisions.

Choose your starting path: this bounded reporting exercise starts from a clear goal. If your real project has several workflows or unresolved requirements, use the goal-driven and spec-driven reference to choose the preparation it needs before accepting a plan.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

sections.title: Start in an isolated practice folder
sections.intro: Use your selected Python 3.12 environment containing the noneditable Harness 1.7.0 wheel.
sections.html:
These practice commands use Bash or another POSIX shell on macOS/Linux. They use shell variables and line continuations. For another shell, have your assistant translate the commands and check the selected runtime before execution.

Follow the course setup first. In the folder containing practice.py, choose a new absolute directory. On macOS, use a canonical parent such as /private/tmp.

Read the command, replace the placeholder, then run it. The helper creates an unfinished report.py, two test files, the CSV, expected output, a local participant registry and a work request. It initializes a disposable Git checkout. It accepts nothing and starts no build.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

sections.title: Ask what may change and how it will be checked
sections.intro: Prepare the draft, then inspect its complete scope before deciding.
sections.html:
Keep the same terminal and PRACTICE value. The task and request live beside the project, outside the checkout whose inputs Harness freezes.

Expect draft, no missing questions and a checkpoint_digest. Read the goal and both test criteria. Only report.py may change. The tests, input, expected outputs, registry and pytest configuration are protected.

If anything is wrong, stop and revise through the supported workflow. Editing the original request after preview does not update the saved task.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

sections.title: Agree to the exact request
sections.intro: Acceptance records the scope you reviewed; execution is another decision.
sections.html:
Copy the full checkpoint_digest from your own preview into PREVIEW_CHECKPOINT. If the displayed request is correct, accept that checkpoint. Expect accepted and a new current checkpoint.

You have not completed the implementation by accepting its scope. In a browser intake, Approve this work request and Keep as draft record the corresponding intent decision; this command practice uses the CLI.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

options.text: Agreement to the displayed scope; execution is still separate.
options.feedback: The saved request is accepted. Starting the local command workers is the next decision.

options.text: The report has already been implemented and checked.
options.feedback: Acceptance records intent, not implementation or test evidence.

sections.title: Give the local commands a bounded go
sections.intro: Inspect the registry before authorizing the prepared offline build.
sections.html:
The practice registry uses two fixed local commands. They make no API or native-model request. Read their configuration and the permitted effects before running the build command.

--allow-external permits these local subprocess participants. It is not a funding grant or a security sandbox. For real model work, review the current participant setup and funding guide; do not infer your route from this fixture.

Expect completed only after the configured checks actually pass. If the command fails, inspect its saved error and journal before choosing a next action.
presenterNotes: Ask the learner to explain the useful result and next decision in their own words.
Keep this offline practice distinct from authorizing real project or model work.

sections.title: Separate a completed task from a trustworthy claim
sections.intro: Read the saved outcome and the tests that support it.
sections.html:
Inspect the saved task. Find the permitted file change, task probe and final probe. In the current course validation, the two reporting test files contain 77 cases. The fixed reviewer only exercises the review protocol; independent assessment of a real implementation remains your responsibility.

Compare the source hash of the input and protected files before and after the build. A passing result supports the cases that ran, rather than every possible input or model.

sections.title: Take the checked result into your browser
sections.intro: Run the completed program against the unchanged six-row CSV.
sections.html:
Move into the practice project. Choose an output path outside that project so the saved work’s input snapshot stays unchanged. Replace the path below with a new filename.

Expect Saved report to …. Open that exact file and check 6 entries, 270 minutes, the project totals and the date range against the CSV. The program refuses to overwrite an existing destination.

sections.title: Leave the work ready to inspect tomorrow
sections.intro: Explain one result, one boundary and the next decision.
sections.html:
These notes stay in this browser. They do not change or approve the Harness task.

Continue with Come back tomorrow to inspect saved work before continuing. Use Decide whether to trust the report to connect a claim to independent evidence.
